summary: Payroll AC-11 HTTP runtime adapter foundation binds existing payroll API DTOs to the repo-native Hyper router/middleware foundation with OpenAPI-aligned JSON responses and explicit non-deployed runtime non-claims.

findings: Runtime adapter is a thin transport boundary: parse DTO JSON, call payroll app functions, serialize response.
No payroll calculation, storage, filing, disbursement, or service call logic was added.
Uses the repo-native Hyper/router/middleware seam rather than adding a second framework.
Exports bounded server config and route manifest so future per-cell binaries can mount the router with body and connection limits.

alternatives_named: bind existing DTOs to repo-native Hyper router foundation
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Repo-native Hyper router binding is the smallest runtime step that advances deployability without adding dependency/framework surface or overclaiming production deployment.
rejected_reasons: A new framework would violate the existing hyper-backbone doctrine and add dependency surface.
A live listener/deployment would require auth, persistence, SLO, and ops evidence not present in this slice.

findings: Serde JSON parse failures return validation envelopes instead of panicking.
Server config fixes a 64 KiB body budget and shorter header/keepalive timeouts for future listener mounting.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed listener exists; tests exercise in-process router dispatch over fixed DTO bodies.

findings.summary: Route dispatch is bounded by the shared router and fixed-size JSON payload handling; no I/O loops or storage calls are introduced.

findings: Public runtime response and route-manifest fields carry data_class annotations.
Health response explicitly marks deployed listener, storage, Workflow dispatch, and statutory filing rails false.
The change is additive: one runtime crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no migrations or external resources.
The route manifest names operation IDs and data-class classifications for later telemetry labels.
Health response exposes router-ready status and non-claim booleans without runtime emission claims.
Payroll AC-11 and D-10 record the runtime adapter foundation and keep deploy/storage/Workflow/filing as future slices.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A payroll HTTP runtime foundation can be useful before cloud integration if it stays router-only and does not claim deployment.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/payroll.json AC-11 and runtime health non-claim tests
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Payroll would keep DTO/OpenAPI contracts but lack executable route bindings for later runtime/server mounting.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Shared Hyper foundation already exists; the missing seam is payroll-specific route binding.

findings: This is the first execution-layer step after metadata/domain/API foundations, while preserving honest non-claims around deployment and persistence.
Names follow payroll run, runtime adapter, route manifest, Hyper foundation, and OpenAPI operation vocabulary.
Payroll spec, OpenAPI meta, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
Runtime-specific code lives in a new payroll runtime crate; API DTOs and app/domain crates remain unchanged.
No new HTTP framework, storage repository, Workflow client, HR/accounting client, audit emitter, filing transport, or deployment artifact was introduced.

No new third-party dependencies were added; runtime uses existing workspace serde/serde_json and repo-native HTTP foundation crates, and dependency-rationales allow-list was updated for adapter-layer use.
Responses use camelCase JSON and align to existing PayrollAccepted and HR leave-impact response OpenAPI shapes; OpenAPI metadata records the runtime adapter addition.
Handlers perform deterministic parse -> app call -> JSON response flow with explicit 400/202/200 status mapping.
